This document avoids `HTML(...)` and raw injected HTML from Python. It shows the
current static surface using chunks, inline expressions, plain text display,
Markdown display, explicit Markdown tables, and matplotlib.

```{python}
from uv_python_runtime import display, Markdown, Text

base_value = 40
display(Text("SURFACE_TEXT_OUTPUT **not bold**"))
display(Markdown("**SURFACE_MARKDOWN_OUTPUT** from explicit Markdown wrapper."))
```

Inline expressions share document state: `{python} "SURFACE_INLINE_VALUE " + str(base_value + 2)`.

```{python}
base_value += 3
print(f"SURFACE_SHARED_STATE {base_value}")
```

The updated value is visible inline too: `{python} base_value`.

```{python}
#| label: tbl-surface-explicit
#| tbl-cap: Dependency-free explicit Markdown table
from uv_python_runtime import display, Markdown

display(Markdown("""
| feature | status |
| --- | --- |
| chunks | supported |
| inline expressions | supported |
| explicit Markdown tables | supported |
| raw Python HTML injection | not used here |
"""))
```

The table reference resolves as @tbl-surface-explicit.

```{python}
#| label: fig-surface-line
#| fig-cap: Inspectable matplotlib figure from surface example
#| fig-alt: Simple line chart generated by uv-python without Jupyter
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt

fig = plt.figure()
ax = fig.subplots()
ax.plot([1, 2, 3], [2, 3, 5], marker="o")
_ = ax.set_title("Surface example")
```

The figure reference resolves as @fig-surface-line.
